en: The man whose son I see is good.
la: Vir cuius fīlium videō bonus est.
explain: _cuius_ is the genitive of _quī_: “of whom, whose”. It is the same for all genders.
distractors: Vir cui fīlium videō bonus est.
_cui_ is dative (“to whom”). “Whose” is genitive: _cuius_.
Vir quem fīlium videō bonus est.
_quem_ is accusative (“whom”). “Whose” is genitive: _cuius_.
Vir quō fīlium videō bonus est.
_quō_ is ablative (“by whom”). “Whose” is genitive: _cuius_.

en: The girl whose mother is coming is good.
la: Puella cuius māter venit bona est.
explain: _cuius māter_ is “whose mother”, the mother of the girl.
distractors: Puella cui māter venit bona est.
_cui_ is dative (“to whom”). “Whose” is genitive: _cuius_.
Puella quam māter venit bona est.
_quam_ is accusative (“whom”). “Whose” is genitive: _cuius_.
Puella quae māter venit bona est.
_quae_ is nominative (“who”). “Whose” is genitive: _cuius_.

en: The man to whom I give the book is good.
la: Vir cui librum dō bonus est.
explain: _cui_ is the dative of _quī_: “to whom, for whom”. He receives the book.
distractors: Vir cuius librum dō bonus est.
_cuius_ is genitive (“whose”). “To whom” is dative: _cui_.
Vir quem librum dō bonus est.
_quem_ is accusative (“whom”). “To whom” is dative: _cui_.
Vir quō librum dō bonus est.
_quō_ is ablative (“by whom”). “To whom” is dative: _cui_.

en: The girl to whom I give water is good.
la: Puella cui aquam dō bona est.
explain: The girl receives the water, so _cui_ (dative). It is the same for all genders.
distractors: Puella cuius aquam dō bona est.
_cuius_ is genitive (“whose”). “To whom” is dative: _cui_.
Puella quam aquam dō bona est.
_quam_ is accusative (“whom”). “To whom” is dative: _cui_.
Puella quā aquam dō bona est.
_quā_ is ablative (“by whom”). “To whom” is dative: _cui_.

en: The sword with which I fight is good.
explain: A tool goes in the ablative, so “with which” is _quō_ (masculine or neuter ablative).
distractors: Gladius quem pugnō bonus est.
_quem_ is accusative. A tool takes the ablative: _quō_.
Gladius cui pugnō bonus est.
_cui_ is dative. A tool takes the ablative: _quō_.
Gladius quae pugnō bonus est.
_quae_ is feminine or plural. _gladius_ is masculine singular: _quō_.

en: The road by which I walk is long.
explain: The road is feminine, and “by which” is ablative: _quā_.
distractors: Via quam ambulō longa est.
_quam_ is accusative. “By which” is ablative: _quā_.
Via quō ambulō longa est.
_quō_ is masculine or neuter ablative. _via_ is feminine: _quā_.
Via cuius ambulō longa est.
_cuius_ is genitive (“whose”). “By which” is ablative: _quā_.

en: The friend with whom I walk is good.
la: Amīcus cum quō ambulō bonus est.
explain: _cum_ takes the ablative. After a relative pronoun it stays a separate word (unlike _mēcum_): _cum quō_.
distractors: Amīcus cum quem ambulō bonus est.
_quem_ is accusative. After _cum_, use the ablative: _quō_.
Amīcus cum cui ambulō bonus est.
_cui_ is dative. After _cum_, use the ablative: _quō_.
Amīcus cum quā ambulō bonus est.
_quā_ is feminine. _amīcus_ is masculine: _quō_.

en: The friends with whom I live are good.
la: Amīcī cum quibus habitō bonī sunt.
explain: The plural dative and ablative of _quī_ is _quibus_. After _cum_ it is ablative.
distractors: Amīcī cum quōs habitō bonī sunt.
_quōs_ is accusative. After _cum_, use the ablative: _quibus_.
Amīcī cum quī habitō bonī sunt.
_quī_ is nominative. After _cum_, use the ablative: _quibus_.
Amīcī cum cuius habitō bonī sunt.
_cuius_ is singular genitive. “With whom” (plural) is _quibus_.

en: The men whose sons fight are good.
la: Virī quōrum fīliī pugnant bonī sunt.
explain: The genitive plural of _quī_ is _quōrum_ (feminine _quārum_): “of whom, whose”.
distractors: Virī cuius fīliī pugnant bonī sunt.
_cuius_ is singular. _virī_ is plural: _quōrum_.
Virī quōs fīliī pugnant bonī sunt.
_quōs_ is accusative (“whom”). “Whose” is genitive: _quōrum_.
Virī quibus fīliī pugnant bonī sunt.
_quibus_ is dative or ablative. “Whose” is genitive: _quōrum_.

en: The women to whom we give water are good.
la: Fēminae quibus aquam damus bonae sunt.
explain: The women receive the water, so dative plural: _quibus_.
distractors: Fēminae quās aquam damus bonae sunt.
_quās_ is accusative. The ones receiving are dative: _quibus_.
Fēminae quōrum aquam damus bonae sunt.
_quōrum_ is genitive (“whose”). “To whom” is dative: _quibus_.
Fēminae quae aquam damus bonae sunt.
_quae_ is nominative. The ones receiving are dative: _quibus_.

en: Rome, which I love, is great.
explain: Names work like any noun: _Rōma_ is feminine, and I love it, so _quam_.
distractors: Rōma, quae amō, magna est.
_quae_ is nominative. I love Rome, so accusative: _quam_.
Rōma, quem amō, magna est.
_quem_ is masculine. _Rōma_ is feminine: _quam_.
Rōma, quod amō, magna est.
_quod_ is neuter. _Rōma_ is feminine: _quam_.
